faqs.question: Is bat removal legal in Midtown Manhattan?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it must be done humanely and in compliance with New York State regulations. Bats are protected species, so removal can only be performed during specific times of year (avoiding maternity season from May-August) and must use exclusion methods that allow bats to leave but not return. Our licensed technicians — licensed by NYS DEC or working under the direct supervision of a licensed applicator — ensure full compliance with all local and state laws.

faqs.answer: We provide transparent pricing before beginning any work and can discuss your situation on a free phone consultation.

faqs.question: How long does the bat exclusion process take?
faqs.answer: The complete bat exclusion process typically takes 3-7 days after the initial inspection. We install one-way exclusion devices that allow bats to exit but not return, monitor the situation to ensure all bats have left, then permanently seal all entry points. Every service includes a service agreement — terms depend on the service and are confirmed on the call.

faqs.question: What are signs of bats in my Midtown building?
faqs.answer: Common signs include squeaking or scratching sounds at dusk or dawn, droppings (guano) accumulating near entry points or on windowsills, brown staining around small openings in walls or rooflines, and seeing bats entering or exiting your building at twilight. Bats can enter through openings as small as 3/8 of an inch, making early detection important.
